$comment: The same intent answered with the wrong menu item, which is the failure this whole suite exists to see. Test
automation writes tests against an implementation; the intent says no test code exists and asks where the risk
sits, which is the other workflow entirely.
It is the pair to correct-route: same oracle, same scope, and only the decision changed, so a scorer that
stopped comparing the menu code would move this case and leave that one alone.
A frozen copy of one case of the live corpus and of the menu it is scored against. The pair (expected, menu)
is the whole input to scoreCase beside the reply, so both are stored here rather than read live: a replay has
to keep scoring the scenario it was derived against after the corpus moves on, and
npm run test:eval-routing-data already holds the live corpus against the shipped menu.

expected.rationale: An epic is finished, no test code exists, and the ask is where risk sits and how much coverage each area deserves. That is test design's whole sentence.

derivation: The action is route and the oracle expects route, so actionCorrect is true. The menu code is TA and the oracle
expects TD, so routeCorrect is false. actionCorrect and routeCorrect are separate fields for exactly this:
answering the right kind of answer and answering it with the right item are two different claims.
decidingTokens is [risk, coverage, epic]. The reason carries "the epic" and neither "risk" nor "coverage", so
tokensFound is 1 and tokensMissed names the two that are absent.
The scope is unchanged from correct-route, so scopeOk stays true: a wrong route can still carry the right
scope, and the two are scored apart because a wrong workflow run against the right epic is a different repair
from a right workflow run against the wrong one.
